articles.title: ENES KANTER FREEDOM: The WNBA says I'm a man. So why is it still afraid to say who is a woman?
articles.summary: The WNBA has made one thing clear: it is convinced that I am a man. The question now is whether Commissioner Engelbert and the WNBA are willing to tell America what makes someone a woman.
articles.body: Ladies and gentlemen, we finally have an answer from the WNBA. Sort of. After months of questions about who is eligible to compete in women's professional basketball, WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert has declared in an official letter that I am not eligible to play in the league. WNBA TELLS CONGRESS THAT ENES KANTER FREEDOM, ROYCE WHITE ARE ‘BOTH MEN’ IN ELIGIBILITY DISPUTE Why? Because Cuckoo Cathy identified me as a man. I was as shocked as you probably are to learn that a league that can't define what a woman is can so confidently identify a man. But apparently, telling me I can't play wasn't enough. Now, the WNBA doesn't even want me in the stands as a paying customer. I believe every woman who steps onto a basketball court deserves the opportunity to compete fairly. I believe female athletes deserve to have their concerns heard, even when their opinions are unpopular. And I believe no athlete should feel pressured to sacrifice her convictions to protect her career. On Wednesday night, I traveled to Atlanta to attend Game 3 of the WNBA Finals. I purchased premium courtside tickets, just like any other basketball fan. But when I arrived, I was informed that I would not be allowed to sit in the seats I purchased. Instead, they decided I would have to watch the game from a private suite and enter through a private entrance, supposedly for my safety. ENES KANTER FREEDOM GOES SCORCHED EARTH ON LEBRON JAMES, NBA WITH NEW REVELATIONS AFTER WNBA FINALS INCIDENT I appreciate the concern for my safety. But I have spent years speaking out against authoritarian regimes that have threatened my life and my family. I am certainly not going to hide in a luxury suite because my presence makes someone uncomfortable. I wanted to sit in the seats I paid for, watch the game, and continue standing up for women in sports. But when I refused to be moved out of sight, security denied me entry. I was escorted away from the arena. For the second time, I was prevented from attending a WNBA game while speaking up for women. The WNBA is apparently more comfortable removing me from its arena than answering the questions I am asking. And those questions begin with Commissioner Engelbert's response to Congressman Marlin Stutzman of Indiana. In her letter, she wrote, "only women are eligible to play in the WNBA and the individuals you cite in your letter are both men." Notice what she did not say. ENES FREEDOM LEAVES WNBA FINALS AFTER SPARRING WITH POLICE OVER SEATING CHANGE AMID SECURITY CONCERNS She did not say that biological males are categorically ineligible to compete in the WNBA. She did not establish a biological standard for eligibility. She simply declared that I am a man and therefore cannot play. Who gave Commissioner Engelbert the authority to determine my identity? What standards did she use to make that determination? And if she can so confidently identify me as a man, why can't the WNBA apply that same clarity to the question of who qualifies as a woman? You cannot have it both ways. The WNBA has reportedly assembled a task force to examine its eligibility policies. Yet we still have no publicly available, definitive policy establishing whether biological males who identify as women can compete in the league. A task force. Meetings. Discussions. And still no clear answer to one of the most basic questions a women's sports league should be able to answer. The women who have spent their entire lives training to compete at the highest level of their sport deserve to know that the rules protecting their opportunities will be applied fairly and consistently. And before that can happen, the rules must be clear. WNBA HAS 'NO IDEA WHAT THEY'RE ABOUT TO FACE,' ENES KANTER FREEDOM SAYS AS LEAGUE TAKES ON TRANS ATHLETE ISSUE That is why I am pursuing the opportunity to compete under the WNBA's rules. I have played professional basketball at the highest level, and I am prepared to pursue a place on a team. If the league believes I am ineligible, it should be able to identify the specific, consistently applied standard that disqualifies me. Instead, the WNBA has created a contradiction. The league knows I should not compete against women. It is willing to say so publicly. Yet it has not clearly explained whether the same biological considerations would disqualify another male athlete who identifies as a woman. Is the league afraid of offending activists? Is it more concerned about political backlash than protecting its own athletes? Or does it simply want to leave the door open for exceptions while keeping someone like me out because I am willing to challenge its reasoning? WNBA COMMISSIONER CATHY ENGELBERT BLAMES THE WRONG PEOPLE FOR ‘SOWING DIVISIVENESS’ IN TRANSGENDER DEBATE I cannot tell you what is happening behind closed doors. But I can tell you what the public has been given. A task force that has produced no clear public standard. A commissioner who can declare who is a man without explaining how she reaches that conclusion. And now, a league that would rather move a vocal fan out of public view than allow him to sit in the seats he purchased. But this fight is about something much bigger than my eligibility or where I sit at a basketball game. It is about freedom. It is about fairness. And it is about the right to have your voice heard, especially when those in power would prefer your silence. ROYCE WHITE EXPLORING LEGAL AVENUES AFTER WNBA TELLS CONGRESS HE IS INELIGIBLE TO PLAY I know what it means to live under a government that punishes people for speaking their minds. I know what it means to have your freedom threatened because you refuse to remain silent. My criticism of authoritarianism has come at a tremendous personal cost, including separation from my family. That is why, when I earned my American citizenship, I changed my last name to Freedom. That was not a publicity stunt. It was a declaration of gratitude, conviction and pride in my country. The fight to preserve freedom became part of my identity. I believe every woman who steps onto a basketball court deserves the opportunity to compete fairly. I believe female athletes deserve to have their concerns heard, even when their opinions are unpopular. And I believe no athlete should feel pressured to sacrifice her convictions to protect her career. Those are freedoms worth defending. REPUBLICAN LAWMAKER BELIEVES THE WNBA SHOULD ADOPT THE OLYMPIC STANDARD FOR WOMEN’S SPORTS Meanwhile, as this debate unfolds, players from the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream have been running off the court before the national anthem, returning shortly after it concludes. I understand that Americans have the freedom to protest. That is one of the things that makes this country extraordinary. But it brings us back to the distinction between having a right and being right. America is not perfect, and it never has been. But this is also a nation where women have fought for and won opportunities that generations before them could scarcely imagine, including the opportunity to become professional athletes, compete on a national stage, and build careers playing the sport they love. When I see athletes walk away from the American flag and an anthem that honors the costly battles fought for our freedom, I see an opportunity being missed. Those freedoms made their opportunities possible, and those opportunities deserve respect and protection. There is a painful irony in watching players leave the court rather than stand for our anthem while the league responsible for protecting their competition seems equally determined to avoid taking a stand on fairness. WNBA ANTHEM CONTROVERSY SPARKS CALLS TO BAR PLAYERS WHO DON'T STAND FROM TEAM USA'S OLYMPIC ROSTER And now, when I show up to ask questions and stand up for those principles, the league wants me out of sight, too. Freedom requires courage. So does fairness. Both demand that we defend principles even when doing so makes people uncomfortable. It requires us to stay in the arena and confront difficult questions about what is true and just rather than running away because we don't like the fight. I have spent much of my life fighting for people whose voices powerful institutions would rather silence. I am not going to stop now simply because the institution in question happens to be a professional basketball league. I am grateful to Congressman Stutzman for demanding answers, and I am glad Commissioner Engelbert finally responded. But her letter raises more questions than it answers. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION If I am ineligible because she says I am a man, then say plainly whether all biological males are ineligible for the same reason. If biological sex is not the determining factor, explain what is. And if the WNBA believes women's sports deserve protection, establish a clear, consistent policy that actually protects them. The WNBA can deny me a spot on the court. It can deny me the seats I purchased. It can even escort me out of the arena. Again. But it cannot make me stop asking questions. And it cannot make me stop fighting for the women whose opportunities, voices, and freedoms deserve to be protected. I did not change my last name to Freedom because I wanted to avoid uncomfortable fights. I changed it because I know how precious freedom is and how easily it can be lost when people are afraid to defend what they know is right. articles.title: Nikola Jokic Blasts Booing Fans, 'Not Welcome Anymore' After Nuggets' Comeback Win vs. Pelicans
articles.summary: Nikola Jokić doesn't want the Denver Nuggets fans who booed the team during Saturday's 141-135 overtime victory to return to Ball Arena.
articles.body:
Nikola Jokić doesn't want the Denver Nuggets fans who booed the team during Saturday's 141-135 overtime victory to return to Ball Arena.

"We got booed at our first home game, and I think those fans who booed us, they don't need to come anymore," Jokić told reporters . "If you guys follow us, you know that we never quit and we've come back from much worse situations. So, if they ask me, they are not welcome anymore."

The Nuggets were down 23 points during the game but rallied for the comeback win after some of the fans expressed their displeasure with the early deficit.

Perhaps there was some leftover frustration from Nuggets fans after the team lost in the first round of the playoffs last season and then dropped its 2026-27 opener by double digits to the Oklahoma City Thunder.

When the Nuggets fell behind by so many points, it seemed like there would be an early losing streak to start the season.

However, Jamal Murray and Jokić had other ideas.

Murray poured in 42 points behind eight three-pointers, while Jokić did a little bit of everything on his way to a triple-double of 35 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists. He is now just 10 triple-doubles behind Russell Westbrook's 209 for the most in NBA history.

The two stars had to do even more on the offensive side because the Nuggets were playing without Cam Johnson, Alpha Diallo, Julian Strawther and Spencer Jones, which could have explained the poor start.

"It was just, you know, nothing goes your way, they're making shots and you're not making shots," Jokić said of the initial deficit. "It was just bad energy and it needs a couple of minutes to go by so you can get out of it."

Denver remains home for its next game against the Golden State Warriors on Monday and should have a chance to build some initial momentum considering its opponent is 0-3 to start the season.

It's safe to say, though, that the fans won't boo quite as loudly this time around if the Nuggets do fall behind given Jokić's comments.

articles.title: Krampelj y Darling se crecen en el último cuarto para dar al Surne Bilbao un trabajado triunfo
articles.standfirst: Entre los dos suman 17 puntos en el último periodo y tumban la resistencia del MoraBanc Andorra
articles.summary: Entre los dos suman 17 puntos en el último periodo y tumban la resistencia del MoraBanc Andorra
articles.body: El Surne Bilbao Basket se ha repuesto una semana después del gran revés encajado ante el Real Madrid (119-84) la pasada jornada y retornó al camino del triunfo a costa de un Morabanc Andorra que plantó cara en un partido de ida y vuelta al que los locales llegaron con más energía. El equipo bilbaíno se afanó de inicio en minimizar los daños que podía generar la estrella andorrana Kyle Kuric, que venía de lograr 26 puntos la pasada jornada contra Breogán, y lo logró en un primer tiempo en el que, sin embargo, no pudo hacer lo propio con Akinjo, el catalizador de la clara ventaja al término del primer cuarto (15-22) para Andorra . El segundo cuarto se desarrolló con los bilbaínos a rebufo del marcador ante un conjunto de los Pirineos que tenía en su mejor momento al gigante ucraniano Pustovyi (2,19) y que no hizo más daño por un bajo porcentaje en los triples que mejoraría en los últimos minutos de este período. En este tramo final previo al descanso también se activaría Bilbao Basket y con Normandas y Somogyi dio la vuelta al luminoso, para conseguir por fin su objetivo de comandar el encuentro (38-37) ante un conjunto andorrano que no tenía intención alguna de dar su brazo a torcer. Surne Bilbao entró como un tiro al tercer cuarto y un 5-0 de parcial le daría ya un margen que no perdería durante todo el encuentro porque la defensa local se convirtió en inescrutable para un equipo visitante que sufriría la lluvia de tres triples seguidos que dieron una ventaja importante a los vascos antes del último cuarto. Ahí apareció la muñeca de Kuric desde el 6,75 (5/6) y Andorra estrechó la diferencia abocando el choque a un final incierto que Krampelj se encargaría de definir con su acierto ofensivo a favor del Surne Bilbao Basket. 88.- Surne Bilbao Basket (15+27+23+23: Frey (8), Vautier (5), Petrasek (9), Normantas (8), Hilliard (11) - cinco inicial -Somogyi (8), Krampelj (20), Hilnason (6), Darling (8), Ansoregi, Duscak y Font (5). 76.- MoraBanc Andorra (22+18+17+19): Akinjo (13), Robertson (4), Ortega, McGriff (6) y Radošević (2) -cinco inicial- Iwundu (5), Pustovyi (14), Kuric (17), Best (6), Mutic (5), Andronikashvili (4), y Owen Aquino. articles.title: NBA star torches fan base after boos rain down after first half: 'They are not welcome anymore'
articles.summary: Nikola Jokic told Denver Nuggets fans who booed at halftime they are "not welcome anymore" after a dramatic 18-point comeback over the Pelicans.
articles.body: The Denver Nuggets are two games into the regular season and three-time NBA MVP Nikola Jokic is already fed up. The Nuggets eked out a 141-135 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Saturday night. Jokic finished with 35 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists. Denver was down 75-57 going into the locker room at halftime. Jokic and the rest of the team heard boos from the fans at the Ball Arena. articles.title: Kerr Calls Out Yaxel Lendeborg with Brutally Honest Quote on 'Very Poor' Awareness in New Video
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has wasted no time making an impression early in his NBA career in large part because he ripped Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Dončić, but his head coach wants him to focus on the defensive side of the ball.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has wasted no time making an impression early in his NBA career in large part because he ripped Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Dončić, but his head coach wants him to focus on the defensive side of the ball.

"The biggest thing is just continuing to learn the NBA," Steve Kerr told reporters after Saturday's 131-122 loss to the Phoenix Suns. "… The defensive side is where I want to see the most improvement, though. His weak-side awareness right now is very poor. And with his size, he should be one of our best defenders at the rim. And right now, he's unaware on the weak-side. And that's an area he really has to improve."

Despite the defensive concerns, Lendeborg has impressed on the offensive end through his first three games.

He has scored in double digits every time he's taken the court, including in Saturday's contest when he poured in 26 points behind 6-of-11 shooting from three-point range. He also grabbed nine rebounds and dished out five assists.

With Stephen Curry (right knee), Brandin Podziemski (low back), Draymond Green (low back) and Al Horford (low back) all sidelined, Lendeborg assumed a larger role and finished with a team-high in scoring.

However, defense was an issue for both him and the team as a whole.

Devin Booker exploded for 43 points and seemingly had an answer every time the Warriors built some momentum.

That Kerr is focused on Lendeborg's defense is notable because opponents will likely look to target him with pick-and-rolls and matchup advantages if he doesn't make strides on that end of the floor.

And they will also likely seek him out if he doesn't back down in the trash-talking department after getting into it with Dončić during the Warriors' opener:

The Michigan product told reporters he "lost all respect" for the Lakers star, going as far as saying he "sucks" and "can't score on me."

He then doubled down and said Dončić is "not Michael Jordan."

Continuing to talk trash like that is going to draw attention, so Lendeborg's defense will be under the spotlight throughout his rookie campaign.

articles.body: El FIATC Girona se mantiene al máximo nivel en casa, donde ha conquistado este domingo su quinta victoria en otros tantos partidos, esta vez al ganar al Asisa Joventut (101-87), con una nueva gran actuación de Mac McClung (23), Jassel Pérez (14) y también Andrzej Pluta (18). El equipo de Moncho Fernández logró, además, el cuarto triunfo consecutivo entre la Liga Endesa y la Copa FIBA Europa y sigue dando pasos adelante. El cuadro de Dani Miret, lastrado por las bajas de Boogie Ellis y Ludde Hakanson, puso fin a una racha de tres victorias entre la ACB y la Liga de Campeones, a pesar del buen partido de Álex Reyes (21), Nico Laprovittola (15) y Ricky Rubio (12). Jassel Pérez partía como líder de la ACB en puntos y en valoración e incluso en recuperaciones tras su exhibición contra el Leyma Coruña (40) y volvió a brillar nada más empezar el encuentro, con ocho puntos en los primeros cuatro minutos (10-8), pero el Girona necesitaba más protagonistas y más juego colectivo. El tanteo inicial dio paso a un parcial visitante de 0-15 que aumentó la ventaja visitante hasta los 12 puntos (13-25). El Joventut despidió el primer período con un 17-27 más un 1-7 en asistencias y un 5-15 en rebotes muy ilustrativos. Los locales tenían un 22% en triples por el 78% visitante en tiros de dos puntos, pero dieron un paso adelante con el inicio del segundo cuarto. El Girona cerró la primera mitad por delante (45-41) y David N'Guessan y Nikola Maric elevaron la renta hasta nueve puntos en el arranque de la segunda parte (52-43), pero el Joventut respondió con un 2-11 bajo la batuta de Ricky (54-52). McClung dejó atrás un momento de dudas personal e individual con cuatro triples consecutivos (63-54) para llegar a los 21 puntos en su cuenta personal y fijar una nueva máxima ventaja (71-54). El parcial ya era de 17-2 y los dos equipos llevaban un 48% y un 22% respectivamente en triples. El Joventut reaccionó con un 1-9 para llegar con cierta esperanza al período definitivo (72-63), pero debía dar un paso adelante en defensa ante un rival que había sumado 55 puntos entre los dos cuartos anteriores. Laprovittola y Reyes lideraron la resistencia en el último período (74-67), pero el Girona mantenía las diferencias y no dejaba que la Penya se acercara demasiado. Los locales acabaron de romper el partido con cuatro triples consecutivos de Dominykas Stenionis y Pluta (95-78) para recuperar la máxima ventaja de 17 puntos. articles.body: La Laguna Tenerife se paseó este domingo en el Santiago Martín para lograr su cuarta victoria del año en la Liga Endesa ante un Monbus Obradoiro que no pudo contener el poderío ofensivo del cuadro aurinegro. En el primer cuarto reinó el equilibrio, en el que los locales comenzaron con un parcial de 8-2 en los primeros dos minutos de juego, pero que los gallegos consiguieron dar la vuelta en minuto cinco, al implantar un 8-10 que avisó a los canaristas de no confiarse si querían sacar un rédito positivo de su feudo ante los recién ascendidos a la categoría, que solo habían perdido un encuentro hasta el momento. articles.title: Jaylen Brown vs. Jayson Tatum Full Revenge-Game Schedule as 76ers, Celtics Stars Trade Viral Quotes
articles.summary: Jayson Tatum said there's no "beef" between him and former teammate Jaylen Brown.
articles.body:
Jayson Tatum said there's no "beef" between him and former teammate Jaylen Brown.

But there should at least be some popcorn in hand for the fans when they face each other this season given the comments they have exchanged.

Here is a look at the full schedule of games between Tatum's Boston Celtics and Brown's Philadelphia 76ers this season:

Brown with an all-time summary of relationship with Tatum

Nov. 10: Boston Celtics at Philadelphia 76ers, 8 p.m. ET

Jan. 21: Philadelphia 76ers at Boston Celtics, 7:30 p.m. ET

Feb. 7: Boston Celtics at Philadelphia 76ers, 7 p.m. ET

March 7: Philadelphia 76ers at Boston Celtics, 1 p.m. ET

These games would have been highly anticipated even without the comments. After all, the Celtics traded Brown to the 76ers this offseason in a move that included Paul George coming to Boston. That stars such as Tatum, LeBron James, Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey will also be on the court makes these games between Eastern Conference rivals appointment viewing.

However, the comments between Tatum and Brown only add another layer.

Tatum posted a video to his YouTube channel and said he was "just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world" when Brown was traded. He added that, "Shams walks over,. He hands me the towel. He's like, 'Yo, put this over your face. Don't react. They just traded him.' I'm like, 'Oh, s--t.' I'm like, 'Where?' He said, 'Philly.' I said, 'We traded him down the street?'"

Yet Brown responded to that video with a cap emoji .

Tatum then opened up about the relationship when he told reporters Friday, "For me, I understand we're in the entertainment business. Me personally, I'm not much of an off the court entertainer type of guy. For me, I don't have any animosity or beef or ill will towards him.

"I think the frustrating part is since he's not with the Celtics anymore, the narrative or conversations haven't been enough about what we've accomplished. All the games we've won, winning a championship, how we've grown together. It's turned into this drama type of thing."

He also said he "called" and "texted" Brown the day he was traded and added, "At this point in our lives, we're too old to be having our relationship discussed X, Y, and Z like on the internet. If there's a conversation to be had, we can definitely have that."

What's more, he said, "This ain't no f--king Shaq and Kobe."

Brown was asked about those comments Saturday and told reporters, "I saw that he said, 'It's no beef.' And I think he's right, there's no beef. Jayson comes from a wonderful family, we've accomplished some great things, he's a hell of a basketball player and he's got a great PR team. It's no beef, but it might be little lamb chops and some gravy, you know what I mean? He should stay ready at all times."

He continued and said, "There's no beef, it should never ever be that. It's just basketball. We're both blessed. But it might be a little lamb chop. We'll be alright."

All of this comes after ESPN's Shams Charania previously reported the off-court relationship between the two stars was "as close to non-existent as you could have" and "a tale of two different people."

So get your popcorn ready because there could be some fireworks when the Celtics face the 76ers this season.

articles.title: Jalen Duren Injury Update, Latest Timeline for Pistons Star to Return from Hamstring Strain
articles.summary: The Detroit Pistons will be without big man Jalen Duren for at least two weeks.
articles.body:
The Detroit Pistons will be without big man Jalen Duren for at least two weeks.

On Sunday, the Pistons announced Duren suffered a right hamstring strain during Friday's win over the Miami Heat and "will be re-evaluated in two weeks."

The early injury this season comes after the 22-year-old was under the spotlight throughout the offseason because of his contract status.

Yet he and the Pistons eventually agreed to a five-year, $200 million deal shortly before the deadline for restricted free agents to sign a qualifying offer. The agreement came on Oct. 1 and not long before Detroit's season opener on Oct. 20.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported "there were fractures built within the player-team relationship during the business of restricted free agency." The process included Duren skipping media day and "hoping for a potential sign and trade," although he eventually agreed to the deal Detroit offered.

This is a disappointing setback for both the player and team considering the Pistons are off to a 2-0 start and Duren looked excellent before the injury.

He finished with 22 points, nine rebounds, one block and one steal in the win over the Boston Celtics and seemed on his way to a double-double with four points, six rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal in just 10 minutes against the Heat until he hurt his hamstring.

His early play figured to draw attention given his contract negotiations, especially since he struggled so much in the team's second-round playoff loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers.

Duren scored fewer than 10 points in four of the seven games in that series and averaged just 7.6 rebounds, which was well below his season average of 10.5.

It seemed like he was putting those struggles behind him in the early going this season, but he will now have to wait at least two weeks before returning to the court.

articles.title: De Larrea se acuerda de sus ancestros: "Ver a Ricky, Sergio y Calderón me hace dar esos pases"
articles.standfirst: El base de los Mavericks fue protagonista ante los medios tras meter 21 puntos en su tercer encuentro en la NBA
articles.summary: El base de los Mavericks fue protagonista ante los medios tras meter 21 puntos en su tercer encuentro en la NBA
articles.body: Después de su fantástica actuación en su tercer partido en la NBA, Sergio De Larrea no quiso olvidarse de sus ancestros en el baloncesto español. De esos bases que marcaron una época con la selección y también abrieron el camino de otros, como él, hacia la mejor Liga del mundo. "Sigo aprendiendo sobre todo de Ricky Rubio, Sergio Rodríguez, José Manuel Calderón... Esos bases a los que observaba mucho en televisión cuando era joven. Quizás haberles visto me lleva a dar estos pases", dijo al ser cuestionado por su capacidad para asistir. El base español, después de no haber anotador en los dos primeros partidos de su carrera en la NBA, se fue hasta los 21 puntos en la derrota frente a los Spurs. Pese a su buen hacer, no se le veía demasiado contento. "Sí, lo estoy, sin duda", dijo con una sonrisa. "Es la primera vez que anoto estos puntos. En los últimos dos partidos fue diferente", aseguró. De Larrea firmó en su tercer partido una de las mejores anotaciones de su carrera. Su tope en la Liga Endesa son los 20 puntos que le hizo al San Pablo Burgos en marzo de este año. En competiciones nacionales, su cima son los 21 que anotó ante el Real Madrid en la Supercopa Endesa de la temporada pasada y que le acabaron dando el MVP del torneo. En la Euroliga, se fue hasta los 23 en un choque del curso pasado ante la Virtus Bolonia. El director de juego de los Mavericks, saliendo desde el banquillo, cumplió con creces en una situación apurada para su equipo, que no contó ni con Cooper Flagg, lesionado de un hombro y ausente para al menos una semana, ni con Kyrie Irving, al que se le dio descanso en el segundo partido en noches consecutivas. Después de volver de 19 meses de baja, no va a correr riesgos. Larry, protagonista ante los medios por su sensacional partido, dijo que aún tiene "muchas cosas por mejorar. Las rotaciones en defensa, estar preparado… Estoy trabajando todos los días para este momento y hoy creo que fue un resultado de este trabajo".

articles.title: Pistons C Jalen Duren strains hamstring, will be re-evaluated in 2 weeks
articles.summary: If he misses two weeks, Duren is expected to be out for Detroit's next six games.
articles.body:
The Detroit Pistons announced that center Jalen Duren is dealing with a right hamstring strain. The center will be re-evaluated in two weeks, according to the team.

Duren picked up the injury in the second quarter of Friday night's win over the Miami Heat. The Detroit center is averaging 13 points, 7.5 rebounds and 2 assists per game early in the 2026-2027 NBA season.

Without Duren in the lineup, Detroit could move Paul Reed from the bench to a starting spot. The Pistons could also move John Collins from power forward to center and give Ronald Holland II a start.

Detroit expects Duren to miss the next six games before re-evaluating him. In that span, the Pistons face the Philadelphia 76ers (twice), New York Knicks, Charlotte Hornets (twice) and Brooklyn Nets.

If the Detroit center is cleared right at the two-week mark, he could return on Nov. 8 at home against the Los Angeles Lakers.

Before getting hurt against Miami, Duren played just 10 minutes. In that time, he shot 2 of 4 for just four points but grabbed six rebounds and three assists.

Reed finished with a double-double, 19 points and 11 boards, off the bench. Holland played a well-rounded game, scoring eight points with five rebounds and four assists in 22 minutes. Detroit could deploy a balanced rotation, working them both in Duren's absence.

Duren was a hot topic over the offseason because he and the Pistons couldn't agree on a contract. While trade rumors swirled, Detroit got the deal done, signing him to a 5-year, $200 million extension that keeps him under contract through the 2030-2031 season.

Detroit will first take the floor without Duren on Sunday as the Pistons put their 2-0 record on the line against the 76ers.

articles.title: Atkinson Calls Out Cavs' Conditioning in New Video After James Harden, Mitchell, Cavs Beat Nets
articles.summary: Two games into the regular season, Cleveland Cavaliers coach Kenny Atkinson feels his team is still shaking out the cobwebs a bit physically.
articles.body:
Two games into the regular season, Cleveland Cavaliers coach Kenny Atkinson feels his team is still shaking out the cobwebs a bit physically.

The Cavs held on to beat the Brooklyn Nets 125-121 after having allowed 41 points in the fourth quarter. Following the game, Atkinson told reporters Cleveland isn't "in elite condition right now, which is kind of normal" (35-second mark).

"Second game, getting your rhythm. We're not there," he said. "I told the guys in the timeout we gotta fight through the fatigue. I thought we had moments of fatigue, but I felt like when I put that last group in to come back, they were sitting for a while. We just weren't locked in or focused."

Jokic says booing fans not welcome in Denver

Brown with an all-time summary of relationship with Tatum

The Cavaliers were up by 11 points with a little over a minute remaining. A long-range jumper from Michael Porter Jr. made it a two-point game with 8.1 seconds remaining, but Cavs guard Sam Merrill spared them what would've been a second straight collapse.

Atkinson's squad led the Philadelphia 76ers by as many as 29 points in its opener Thursday night before wilting in the second half. The Sixers prevailed 114-106.

The coach spoke matter-of-factly in Saturday's press conference rather than in a tone that challenged his players. Game 2 of an 82-game season isn't the time to begin panicking.

But Atkinson's remarks are likely to raise some eyebrows given Cleveland is mostly running it back with a veteran-laden core. The manner of the Cavs' 2026 playoff exit would've seemingly reinforced the need to remain engaged for four quarters as well.

Players often train and practice with the idea of being at their best for the business end of the regular season and into the playoffs. Nobody expects the Cavaliers to be at their peak in late October.

Still, it's a little surprising that Atkinson would cite conditioning as a complicating factor already.

articles.title: NBA insider reveals real reason Lakers didn't trade Dalton Knecht to Bucks for Jericho Sims
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers were trying to get some value out of Dalton Knecht before cutting him. They were unable to and it has been revealed what the cost woul...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers knew they would have to make a roster decision before the regular season began. After making numerous moves over the summer, the team found itself one player over the roster limit, meaning someone would have to be let go.

Dalton Knecht appeared to be the most likely candidate if the Lakers reached that point. Before making a final decision, LA explored trade options to trim the roster.

"My understanding is a consolidation trade. Obviously, it would be two-for-one, three-for-one, or three-for-two is a little more complicated," Lakers insider Jovan Buha said. "So I think the most straightforward one would be two-for-one…And depending on the configuration of the trade, it could be a version of two of the back-end guys, let's say Dalton Knecht and Jaden Hardy, for a backup center."

Just before the deadline to make roster cuts, the Lakers entered trade discussions with the Milwaukee Bucks about a potential deal involving center Jericho Sims.

"League sources say that the Lakers and Bucks have held exploratory trade discussions on a framework that would ship former first-round selection Dalton Knecht to Milwaukee (along with second-round draft capital) in exchange for big man Jericho Sims," NBA insider Jake Fischer wrote on the Stein Line.

The Lakers ultimately did not complete the deal, with the draft compensation reportedly becoming a sticking point.

"The Bucks had briefly talked through what Los Angeles would want but were unwilling to trade center Jericho Sims straight up for Knecht and wanted multiple second-round picks or a pick swap. This was a price the Lakers were unwilling to meet. Maybe going across the country and being back on the East Coast will be beneficial for Knecht to reinvent himself," NBA insider Brett Siegel wrote.

Ultimately, letting go of Knecht and absorbing the financial cost may have been the better option for Los Angeles. The Lakers have limited draft capital, and including multiple second-round picks or a pick swap in the deal would have further depleted their assets. Given Knecht's uncertain trade value, the Lakers may not have viewed the additional cost as worthwhile.

Things had not been the same between Los Angeles and Knecht since the failed trade during his rookie season. In the end, the Lakers chose not to complete a deal that could have addressed their need for a backup center because they were unwilling to meet Milwaukee's reported asking price.

articles.title: NBA champ takes issue with Obama's pitch to Michigan voters amid hotly contested Senate race
articles.summary: Kyle Kuzma fired back at Barack Obama's rally pitch for Abdul El-Sayed, saying Michiganders care about poverty and cost of living, not religion.
articles.body: Kyle Kuzma, a one-time NBA champion and current Milwaukee Bucks forward, pushed back on former President Barack Obama’s glowing remarks about Sen. articles.title: Joel Embiid Injury Update, Latest on 76ers Star's Status After Comments on Playing in Back-to-Back
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star Joel Embiid will miss Sunday's game against the Detroit Pistons.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star Joel Embiid will miss Sunday's game against the Detroit Pistons.

The team ruled him out with plantar fasciitis management.

This comes after Embiid struck an optimistic tone about playing in the second part of Philly's back-to-back. He had 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists in Saturday's 127-116 win over the Milwaukee Bucks.

Following the game, the seven-time All-Star joked to reporters they should "put pressure" on the Sixers to give him the green light for Sunday:

The 2025-26 regular season was another injury-filled one for Embiid, who played just 38 games. He appeared in just 19 games last season and 39 in the year before.

It looked as if he'd be healthy in the playoffs, but he had an emergency appendectomy on April 9, just before the end of the regular season. Recovery from the surgery forced him to miss the first three games of the Sixers' opening-round series against the Boston Celtics, but he returned in Game 4 and helped Philadelphia close out the series in seven games.

Embiid had a monster Game 7 against Boston, posting 34 points, 12 boards and six assists.

Unfortunately, injuries struck again ahead of Game 2 against the New York Knicks in the second round. Embiid was ruled out of the matchup because of right hip soreness and a right ankle sprain. He was back for Game 3, but it wasn't enough to avoid a sweep.

The offseason additions of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown will lessen the reliance on Embiid in the regular season. VJ Edgecombe proved as a rookie he can shoulder some of the scoring and rebounding burden as well.

But the Sixers already lost backup center Ariel Hukporti for the season. That leaves Adem Bona as the primary option at the 5 whenever Embiid is unavailable.

Given the lack of depth at the position, Philly will probably remain very proactive in terms of managing Embiid's workload.

articles.title: Eterno Llull: récord histórico de partidos en la ACB con un mismo club
articles.standfirst: Ha jugado su encuentro 690 con el Real Madrid, superando la plusmarca del legendario Juan Carlos Navarro con el Barcelona
articles.summary: Ha jugado su encuentro 690 con el Real Madrid, superando la plusmarca del legendario Juan Carlos Navarro con el Barcelona
articles.body: Sergio Llull ha saltado a la cancha en el segundo cuarto del partido que el Real Madrid está jugando en el Barris Nord ante el iLerna Lleida y se ha convertido en el jugador que más partidos ha disputado con un mismo equipo en la historia de la ACB. El base menorquín se encontraba igualado con otra leyenda, Juan Carlos Navarro, que jugó 689 con el Barcelona y hoy le ha superado al acumular ya 690. Y eso otros 11 que disputó con el Manresa, los primeros de su carrera. El capitán blanco, que sale casi a récord por partido, llegó a los 700 encuentros en la ACB la semana pasada frente al Surne Bilbao Basket. Es el sexto jugador que llega a esa cifra. Por delante, su excompañero Felipe Reyes, Rafa Jofresa, Nacho Rodríguez, Marcelinho Huertas y Nacho Azofra. Todos ellos pasaron por varios equipos o no tuvieron etapas tan longevas como la de Llull en el Madrid, que acumula ya 21 temporadas en el club blanco. Camino de los 39 años, que cumplirá el 15 de noviembre, el base todavía no se ha estrenado esta campaña en la Euroliga, pero sí es un fijo en la Liga Endesa, donde ha participado en los cinco encuentros disputados hasta ahora para firmar nuevos récords o engordar los que ya posee. Aunque su físico ya no es el que era, Llull sigue confirmando que puede ofrecer momentos puntuales de calidad. En la última jornada fue el mejor del Madrid en la aplastante victoria contra el Surne Bilbao terminando con 19 puntos y 5/9 en triples en sólo 12:37 minutos en pista. Más allá de sus estadísticas, es su ascendencia y su ejemplo para el vestuario lo más valioso para el equipo. Los galones son suyos.

articles.standfirst: El base taronja fue un día más el mejor de su equipo con 18 puntos, 5 rebotes y 4 asistencias
articles.summary: El base taronja fue un día más el mejor de su equipo con 18 puntos, 5 rebotes y 4 asistencias
articles.body: El Valencia Basket se impuso este domingo en el Roig Arena al Kosner Baskonia con un inspirado TJ Shorts, que terminó el partido con 18 puntos y 4 asistencias, y que fue clave para superar a un conjunto baskonista que plantó cara hasta el final a pesar de contar con solo ocho jugadores disponibles. El Valencia Basket golpeó primero. Una vez superados los primeros minutos de imprecisiones, el conjunto 'taronja' subió su ritmo de juego y aprovechó las complicaciones físicas del Baskonia para encontrar una ventaja que fue aumentando hasta los dobles dígitos. Los puntos en la pintura de Jasiel Rivero y Nikola Mirotic y el acierto exterior de Armoni Brooks valieron un parcial de 10-0 que obligó al banquillo baskonista a pedir un tiempo muerto en busca de soluciones (21-9, min.7). El respiro le vino bien a un Baskonia que respondió con dos triples seguidos, pero que era incapaz de cerrar su pintura y de parar a TJ Shorts, que volvió a ampliar la distancia a los 8 puntos al final del primer parcial. El Baskonia consiguió mejorar su cara defensiva y, con un juego más lento, empezó a sentirse cómodo sobre la pista y obligó al Valencia Basket a escoger malos tiros que no acertaba. Así, fue capaz de acercarse a solo dos puntos con una canasta de bella factura de Stefan Joksimovic y un triple de DJ Stewart en la esquina (31-29, min.16). El tiempo muerto fue entonces para el Valencia Basket, que volvió a despegar a base de los triples de Dylan Osetkowski y Armoni Brooks. Un triple de Osetkowski sirvió para que TJ Shorts rompiera el récord de más asistencias seguidas sin perder un balón con 21 pases de canasta, superando la cifra de 20 que repartió Toñín Llorente en la temporada 99/00. El parcial de 8-0 desconectó de nuevo al Baskonia, que, aún así, se agarró al partido con la última acción de la primera parte gracias al talento de Joksimovic dejando la distancia en solo 6 puntos. Ese triple le cambió la cara al conjunto vitoriano, que mantuvo su acierto nada más arrancar la segunda parte. Un triple de AJ Lawson y las canastas de Kenneth Faried y Joksimovic le dieron la primera ventaja del partido al Baskonia, que, por primera vez, empezaba a generarle dudas a su rival (41-43, min. 22). El Valencia Basket respondió a base de los triples de Mirotic y Kameron Taylor, pero el Baskonia tenía una confianza mayor que en el primer acto y era capaz de devolver los golpes a pesar de su corta rotación. De hecho, el Valencia Basket tuvo que agarrarse al talento de TJ Shorts para hacer buena su velocidad y también su acierto para recuperar el control del marcador (59-53, min.30). En el último cuarto, con el paso de los minutos y con un pequeño parcial de 6-2 de salida, parecía que el Valencia Basket empezaba a mandar a la lona al Baskonia, pero el carácter de los jugadores y el acierto individual de hombres como Stewart y Faried y la capacidad para sacar tiros libres seguían apretando el marcador y dejándolo todo abierto (67-65, min. 35). Una vez más, el Valencia Basket confiaba su camino a TJ Shorts, que dejó su impacto con una asistencia para Neal Sako y con una canasta que además llevó consigo una técnica para el entrenador del Baskonia, Velimir Perasovic. Con el viento a favor y con 5 puntos seguidos de Sako, el equipo valenciano recuperó el dominio del juego y del marcador y ya con dobles dígitos de ventaja, puso la suficiente tierra de por medio para terminar de noquear al Baskonia con solo dos minutos por jugar. 84 - Valencia Basket (27+14+18+25): Shorts (18), Taylor (8), Corbalán (2), Osetkowski (6), Sako (15) -cinco inicial- Gueye (-), Saint-Supéry (2), Brooks (13), Puerto (-), Rivero (10), Cárdenas (5), Mirotic (5). 75 - Kosner Baskonia (19+16+18+22): Baugh (9), Spagnolo (3), Stewart (19), Frisch (12), Faried (9) -cinco titular- Lawson (11), Joksimovic (10), Kurucs (-), Sedekerskis (-), Santos (2). articles.title: WNBA Finals: League reportedly unsure where or when Game 6 will be held due to fan demand, scheduling complications
articles.summary: The Dream have played all their home playoff games at State Farm Arena.
articles.body:
The WNBA Finals are guaranteed to go to a Game 6, but that development comes with a significant problem: As of Sunday afternoon, no one knows where or when that game will be played.

The WNBA, NBA, Golden State Valkyries, Atlanta Dream and Atlanta Hawks are all trying to figure out the best solution to that problem, with a WNBA spokesperson telling ESPN, "We will continue to explore all options."

The main issue revolves around the Dream's usual home arena, Gateway Center Arena. That stadium holds just 3,500 people, the smallest stadium capacity in the league.

With interest in the Dream high during the team's playoff run, the team has played every home playoff game at State Farm Arena to meet fan demand. State Farm Arena — where the Hawks play their home games — holds 17,000 fans. The Dream sold out that arena for both Game 3 and Game 4 of the Finals.

That arrangement, however, has already been tested this postseason. With the NBA regular season in full swing, Games 3 and 4 of the WNBA Finals had to be altered so the Dream could play both games at State Farm Arena. The WNBA moved up Game 3 by one day to ensure the Dream could play there. Game 4 was moved to much earlier in the day so that both the Dream and Hawks could play at the stadium on the same day.

While the WNBA could try similar strategies for Game 6, nothing has been decided yet. As of Sunday afternoon, Game 6 is supposed to be played Thursday, Oct. 29 at 8 p.m. ET. That same day, the Hawks are scheduled to take on the Cleveland Cavaliers at State Farm Arena at 7 p.m. ET.

To try and get around that, the WNBA has reportedly offered to shift both Game 6 and a possible Game 7 to different dates to ensure Game 6 could be held at State Farm Arena and that both teams would have adequate time to rest ahead of a possible Game 7, per ESPN. If the series goes to a Game 7, it would be held at the Chase Center in San Francisco.

That proposal would involve Game 6 being held Friday, Oct. 30. If a Game 7 was needed, it would be moved from Saturday, Oct. 31 to Tuesday, Nov. 3.

In order for that proposal to go into effect, both the Dream and Valkyries would have to approve those changes.

While playoff scheduling has been a significant issue for the Dream this season, it will be far less of a barrier in the future. Starting next season, the Dream will play their home games at State Farm Arena, which should lead to — presumably — no scheduling conflicts with the Hawks.

articles.title: New Rumors on WNBA Finals Schedule Conflicts for Angel Reese's Dream, Valkyries with Warriors, Hawks
articles.summary: Once again, the WNBA is facing major uncertainty about where an Atlanta home game will be played, with a Game 6 now guaranteed in the city.
articles.body:
Once again, the WNBA is facing major uncertainty about where an Atlanta home game will be played, with a Game 6 now guaranteed in the city.

According to ESPN's Alexa Philippou and Ramona Shelburne , "Nobody knows where or even when the game will be played despite a furious round of negotiations spilling into Sunday between the WNBA, NBA, Valkyries, Dream and Atlanta Hawks."

The Dream hosted Games 3 and 4 at the State Farm Arena after negotiations with the Hawks and compromises made by both sides, with their own home arena—the Gateway Center Arena—only having a capacity of 3,500.

But according to ESPN's report, "With the Hawks hosting the Cleveland Cavaliers at State Farm the night of Game 6, along with other scheduling complications, the situation is more complex than what the leagues dealt with earlier in the series and could have millions of dollars of impact on both leagues."

At this point, the Dream seem resigned to the possibility of playing in front of just 3,500 fans.

"We are waiting to hear from the league if any changes can be made to allow us to play in State Farm Arena," the team said in a statement. "If not, the game will be played in Gateway Center Arena."

Games 3-4 were able to be played in the State Farm Arena after the WNBA shifted Game 3 up by a day, while the Hawks agreed to holding a doubleheader with the Dream on Saturday for Game 4.

Game 6 seems to be more complicated, with both the Hawks and Cavs on the second leg of a back-to-back that night, though the NBA is exploring its options.

Per ESPN's report, the league "has been working with the Hawks and Cavaliers to determine if Thursday's game could be switched to an alternate date—or even to Cleveland. While some stakeholders feel the onus should be on the NBA to move its regular-season game so the WNBA Finals can be prioritized, there has been pushback from others that the domino effects of moving that game are too complicated."

Another option would be delaying Game 6 until Friday, Oct. 30 and Game 7 to Tuesday, Nov. 3, per ESPN, though both teams would need to approve such an option. The Valkyries reportedly have some concerns about adding three days between both Games 5-6 and again between Games 6-7, but said in a statement they would "fully support what's best for the league and will stand behind whatever it decides."

Nov. 3 is an election day, a date the NBA has recently avoided scheduling, but the Golden State Warriors already have home games scheduled for Nov. 1-2.

Long story short—there are a lot of moving pieces that need to be properly sorted before the Game 6 puzzle can be solved.

articles.title: ‘Worst Talent Evaluator in the NBA,’ ‘No Worse Coach for a Young Player’ — Hoops World Reacts As Steve Kerr Criticizes Warriors Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg
articles.summary: Steve Kerr critiqued rookie Yaxel Lendeborg’s game after Saturday’s 131-122 loss to the Phoenix Suns, on a night the forward scored a season-high 26 points....
articles.body:
Steve Kerr critiqued rookie Yaxel Lendeborg's game after Saturday's 131-122 loss to the Phoenix Suns, on a night the forward scored a season-high 26 points. The Golden State Warriors head coach's comments drew pushback online, and Detroit Pistons journalist Aaron Johnson was among those who took issue with them.

The loss dropped Golden State to 0-3. Playing for the third time in four days, the Warriors rested Stephen Curry (right knee), Draymond Green, Al Horford and Brandin Podziemski (all low back), and Lendeborg played a team-high 36 minutes.

How Steve Kerr's Assessment of Yaxel Lendeborg Caused a Stir

Kerr's critique began on the offensive end. "There was a play in the first half where he got free, and then he launched himself into (Khaman) Maluach… That's gotta be a pull-up jumper, that's gotta be a Euro step, that's gotta be kick it out. In college, you can do that. But this is a different league."

"He'll learn. He's playing a ton. He's going to get all these reps. We're going to keep showing him film. He'll get better and better," Kerr added.

The Warriors coach didn't stop there. "His weak-side awareness right now is very poor. With his size, he should be one of our best defenders at the rim."

A clip of the answer circulated overnight, and the criticism carried into Sunday. Posting Sunday morning, Johnson took aim at both the answer and the circumstances around it.

"Rather than speak highly of him, he throws his rookie under the bus and spends the bulk of his minute long answer critiquing him. Maybe don't have all your top players take a night off less than a week into the season and throw said rookie out there with end of bench and two-way players."

Kerr's answer did open with praise for the first-year forward, though. "Yeah, he's fearless, he's huge, and he's got a great skill set. He can dribble, pass and shoot."

Content creator Jim Park, who posted shortly after the game, focused on how Kerr has used the rookie. He wrote that the coach "leaves Yaxel on an island to protect a 4G lineup at center, knowing full well that he has defensive issues. Please explain to me how this makes any sense."

"Steve Kerr is the worst talent evaluator in the NBA and the master of misusing pretty much every single player he's ever 'coached…' Kerr is the only fraud in the NBA who can't scout the talents of his own players and forces them into positions where they don't belong," he added .

One fan went further, writing , "Kerr was asked what he's most impressed with and he spent most of the answer nitpicking… No worse coach for a young player to play for."

Lendeborg has drawn attention for his own comments this season, after trading words with Luka Dončić during the Warriors' Oct. 21 opener, a 127-105 loss to the Los Angeles Lakers.

Another fan pictured the rookie's next news conference, echoing a phrase Lendeborg used about the Lakers star: "Yaxel: I've lost all respect for Coach Kerr."

Another fan focused less on what Kerr said than on where he said it: "Always a good idea to coach through the media."

The same fan followed up minutes later: "It doesn't matter if it's true or not. It doesn't matter if the player did it first. Keep it in house."

Not everyone saw a problem with it. Another fan wrote , "I like how if Yaxel is going to tell it how it is and speak so candidly in interviews, then Kerr is going to do the same when it comes to Yaxel."

Lendeborg shot 9-of-19 from the field and 6-of-11 from 3-point range on Saturday, adding 9 rebounds and 5 assists, and finished plus-5 in a nine-point loss. Through three games, he is averaging 18.7 points, 8.3 rebounds and 4.3 assists.

Golden State visits the Denver Nuggets on Monday, then faces the Minnesota Timberwolves on the road Wednesday before hosting the Lakers on Oct. 30.

articles.title: El Unicaja aplica la ley del 100 en Lugo
articles.standfirst: Desplegó todo su poder ofensivo para acabar con la resistencia del Río Breogán
articles.summary: Desplegó todo su poder ofensivo para acabar con la resistencia del Río Breogán
articles.body: El Unicaja sacó adelante una visita complicada al Pazo dos Deportes de Lugo. Los malagueños se impusieron al Río Breogán por 90-103 después de mandar durante buena parte del encuentro y, sobre todo, saber responder cada vez que los locales amenazaron con volver al partido. Amine Noua, con 18 puntos, 6 rebotes y 24 de valoración, fue el más destacado de los de Txus Vidorreta. Kendrick Perry, con 24 puntos y 6 asistencias, volvió a ser decisivo. El Breogán arrancó mejor. Kalinoski fue el principal argumento ofensivo de un Unicaja al que le costó entrar en el partido, pero los malagueños fueron creciendo con el paso de los minutos. Un parcial de 0-9 cambió por completo el escenario y puso al equipo de Vidorreta por delante (7-12). El encuentro entró entonces en un intercambio de golpes en el que Mavra y Francis Alonso mantenían al conjunto gallego cerca. Barreiro encontró también el aro desde fuera, aunque Alonso respondió sobre la bocina para dejar el 24-26 al término del primer cuarto. El segundo periodo fue otra historia. El Unicaja empezó a encontrar con mayor facilidad sus tiros y, además, elevó el nivel defensivo. Hunt hizo daño y obligó a Luis Casimiro a parar el partido con 26-33. El Breogán reaccionó con un 5-0, pero los malagueños no perdieron la calma. Perry y Kalinoski castigaron desde el triple y la ventaja volvió a crecer. Ahí llegó el mejor momento del Unicaja. Dos tiros libres de Hunt y los triples consecutivos de Noua y Perry completaron un parcial de 0-13 que llevó el marcador hasta el 36-52. El Breogán consiguió frenar la sangría antes del descanso y recortó algo la diferencia, aunque los visitantes se marcharon a vestuarios con una renta cómoda (47-59). Los lucenses volvieron a salir con otra marcha tras el descanso y llegaron a situarse por debajo de los diez puntos. Fue entonces cuando apareció Noua. El francés volvió a darle energía al Unicaja y los malagueños recuperaron el control hasta colocarse 56-71. El partido, sin embargo, estaba lejos de quedar resuelto. Alonso y Mavra volvieron a tirar del Breogán y un parcial de 10-2 dejó a los locales con opciones (71-79). Perry y Pantzar aparecieron en el momento oportuno para evitar que la reacción fuera a más y el Unicaja encaró el último cuarto con once puntos de ventaja (71-82). Los de Vidorreta tuvieron que trabajar hasta el final. Noua volvió a sacar petróleo con un 2+1 para colocar el 73-87, pero el Breogán seguía insistiendo. Brankovic redujo diferencias y Kravish se encargó de mantener al Unicaja por encima de los diez puntos. Hasta que llegó el último intento local. Un triple de Aranitovic y dos tiros libres de Brown pusieron el 88-92 y encendieron el Pazo. El Unicaja podía haber empezado a sufrir, pero encontró la respuesta en una conexión que funcionó durante toda la noche: Perry asistió a Kravish y el pívot anotó cuatro puntos consecutivos para devolver la tranquilidad (88-96). articles.title: Nets to be without lottery pick against Pacers
articles.summary: The Nets are slated to miss Mikel Brown Jr on Sunday night.
articles.body:
The Brooklyn Nets have been one of the premier teams to watch when it comes to some of the younger stars in the league, given their vast number of first-round picks over the last few seasons. The likes of Egor Demin, Danny Wolf, Nolan Traore, amongst others were the names to make their debuts last season, and this year brought another name to the Barclays Center: Mikel Brown Jr.

Brown was selected with the sixth pick in the 2026 NBA draft and has been a key fixture for Jordi Fernandez this season, appearing in both of Brooklyn's opening matches, in which he's averaged seven points and four assists. These numbers are a far cry from what he was producing during his lone year at Louisville, but they're not exactly bad for someone who is still adapting to life in the NBA.

Brown to miss Sunday's match against the Pacers

But it appears that Brown's playing streak will come to an end on Sunday night, as according to the NBA's injury report, the Nets have listed him as OUT due to a back injury.

However, there's no reason to worry about the rookie's condition, as according to ClutchPoint's Erik Slater, Brown's absence against the Pacers is purely a preventative measure.

Injuries haven't been unusual for the rookie; he suffered a minor ankle injury earlier in the year, but it seems to have subsided.

Tip-off between the Nets and Pacers is slated for 6:00 p.m. EST.

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard Injury Update, Latest on Raptors Star's Status amid Recent 'Greatness' Comments
articles.summary: Toronto Raptors star forward Kawhi Leonard downplayed any concerns about when he will be able to ramp up to full game shape, and now he's shutting things down completely.
articles.body:
Toronto Raptors star forward Kawhi Leonard downplayed any concerns about when he will be able to ramp up to full game shape, and now he's shutting things down completely.

After playing 24 minutes in Wednesday's season opener and declaring , "You can't rush greatness," Leonard is set to miss Sunday night's game against the Minnesota Timberwolves due to knee swelling, the team announced .

Leonard scored 23 points on 5-of-17 shooting in Wednesday's 135-92 win over the Chicago Bulls. He followed that up with a 16-point performance on 7-of-20 shooting in 28 minutes in Friday's 112-102 win over the Washington Wizards.

After the season opener, Leonard was asked if he had a target date for when he'll play a full allotment of minutes, and he replied , "I don't put targets. You can't rush greatness. Whenever the medical thinks I could push forward, and I'm feeling great— whatever numbers we're looking at, or they're looking at, then that's when that time will come. I'm just happy to be out there and try to do the best I can with my minutes."

Leonard's injury history has been well-documented, as he hasn't played in 70 or more games in a season since the 2016-17 campaign. At 35 years old, the two-time NBA champion's main goal is to be healthy in time for the playoffs, so the Raptors will be cautious with his ramp-up period.

Without Leonard in the lineup, more minutes will be available for second-year swingman Collin Murray-Boyles and rookie forward Allen Graves. Leonard's next chance to suit up will be on Wednesday against the Orlando Magic.

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard scratched late for Timberwolves-Raptors with swelling in left knee
articles.summary: The Raptors announced Leonard as a late scratch. The swelling is not in the same knee that's required reconscructive surgery.
articles.body:
The Toronto Raptors have ruled out Kawhi Leonard for Sunday's game against the Minnesota Timberwolves due to swelling in his left knee .

The Raptors announced Leonard as a late scratch in the hour before the scheduled tip. They didn't provide further details about his injury beyond noting the swelling in his knee.

Irritation in his left knee prompted the Clippers to send Leonard home from a road trip in January when he played for Los Angeles last season. He was able to return to the Clippers lineup after missing three games.

The swelling is not in the same knee that required reconstructive surgery. Leonard has previously sustained tears to the ACL and meniscus in his right knee, causing him to miss significant time.

The Raptors and their fans are certainly hoping Leonard's knee swelling doesn't linger and that he's able to return to the lineup soon.

Leonard rejoined the Raptors via trade this offseason, eight seasons removed from leading the franchise to its first and only NBA championship. If healthy, he and All-Star Scottie Barnes form one of the NBA's best two-way tandems on the wing and the anchor of what Toronto hopes is a championship contender.

The Raptors got off to a 2-0 start in Leonard's first games back with wins over the Bulls and Wizards. Leonard averaged 19.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 3.5 steals in those two games, but struggled with his shot while shooting 12 of 37 (32.4%) from the field.

After playing the Timberwolves, the Raptors have back-to-back games against the Magic this week before facing the Lakers on Sunday.

articles.title: 76ers deny Joel Embiid's push to play in back-to-back games, opt to rest him due to injury management vs. Pistons
articles.summary: Joel Embiid dropped a triple-double on Saturday night in the 76ers' win over the Bucks.
articles.body:
Joel Embiid's pressure campaign didn't work.

The Philadelphia 76ers sat their star big man on Sunday for their matchup with the Detroit Pistons due to right foot plantar fasciitis management. The contest is the team's first back-to-back of the season, following Saturday's 127-116 win over the Milwaukee Bucks.

Embiid appeared to know this decision was coming, too, and he tried to get out in front of it.

"I actually want to play tomorrow, so can you guys put pressure on them?" Embiid said on Saturday night, via ESPN's Kris Rhim . "... I want to play tomorrow, so start writing articles and put pressure on them so they'll let me play."

It was a good effort, but the 76ers' brass wasn't swayed. Based on Embiid's injury history, and the fact that Sunday's contest is just the Sixers' fourth of the season, it's easy to understand why.

Embiid hasn't played in more than 40 games in a single season since the 2022-23 campaign, and he's averaged only 49 games a season in his decade in the league. He played in only 38 last season due to a knee injury, an oblique injury and more.

At this stage in Embiid's career, his health is something the 76ers have to work hard to manage. So far this season, he's been great. Embiid recorded the 10th triple-double of his career Saturday night in the 76ers' win over the Bucks with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. He's helped Philadelphia get off to a 3-0 start, including a season-opening win over the defending champion New York Knicks.

The 76ers also ruled VJ Edgecombe, Dominick Barlow, Jabari Walker and Tacko Fall out for Sunday's contest due to various injuries, leaving them short at the position. Walker left Saturday's win early with a left knee issue.

Regardless, the 76ers clearly aren't willing to push Embiid to play in back-to-back contests when they don't have to. Now, Embiid will have to keep trying to plead his case as the season moves on.

articles.title: Dalton Knecht Explains Choosing Knicks Contract amid Rumored Interest from Wolves, More
articles.summary: Following his release from the Los Angeles Lakers last week, Dalton Knecht decided to join the defending champions.
articles.body:
Following his release from the Los Angeles Lakers last week, Dalton Knecht decided to join the defending champions.

The former first-round pick in the 2024 NBA draft signed a two-way deal with the New York Knicks over the weekend. Discussing the deal, Knecht said he felt the Knicks gave him the "best opportunity."

"It just felt like the best opportunity. I talked to the coaching staff, known them for awhile, so it was good," he said. "Thought this would be a great fit, and I'm excited to be here."

The Knicks weren't the only team interested in the former SEC Player of the Year, as the Minnesota Timberwolves, Sacramento Kings and Toronto Raptors reportedly eyed him as well.

Ultimately, New York had an "aggressive" pursuit, according to SNY's Ian Begley , and that was enough to land Knecht.

Knecht had a promising rookie year with the Lakers, averaging 9.1 points per game in 78 contests, but things quickly changed last year. He only played 10.2 minutes per game and was nearly out of the rotation by the end of the season.

It will be hard for Knecht to find minutes on a talented Knicks team, but New York clearly sees potential in him.

The Philadelphia 76ers have not been a great rebounding team early in the 2026-27 season and were absolutely crushed on the boards by the Detroit Pistons during Sunday's 106-93 loss.

Sunday's issues—Detroit out-rebounded the Sixers by a stunning 54-37 margin, pulling down 15 offensive boards alone—weren't a huge surprise. Joel Embiid didn't play on the second half of a back-to-back, power forwards Jabari Walker and Dom Barlow were out with injuries and backup center Ariel Hukporti was already lost for the season with a ruptured Achilles.

The Sixers have struggled with depth down on the block to start the season, though the team is still 3-1 overall. But fixing the rebounding issues may not be as simple as going up and grabbing the ball with two hands off the rim more times than the other team does it.

articles.title: Knicks make unfortunate NBA history not seen from defending champion in 15 years
articles.summary: Jalen Brunson and the Knicks join the 2011-12 Mavericks led by Dirk Nowitzki in an unfortunate NBA record to their defending champion reign.
articles.body:
Defending NBA champions tend to have targets on their backs at the start of the season. Every squad in the league wants to batter down the group that hoisted the Larry O'Brien trophy just a season prior. The New York Knicks , led by Jalen Brunson, are no different. In fact, after their 111-102 loss against the Orlando Magic , they joined the 2011-12 Dallas Mavericks on the wrong side of NBA history. This unfortunate feat has not been seen in the association for a little over 15 years.

Knicks join Mavericks in unfortunately historic NBA feat after loss to Magic

The Knicks did everything in their power to beat the Magic. Jalen Brunson and Co. popped off in the first half. In the first quarter, they scored 28 points while allowing the Magic only 21. The Knicks followed up with a second-quarter slip, scoring only 24 points while the Magic got 27.

All was seemingly going according to plan for the Knicks and Brunson. By the third quarter, the two squads tied the quarter with 23 points apiece. Then, a collapse of absolutely historic proportions happened. The Magic rallied to score 40 points in the fourth quarter. The Knicks? They only got 27 points.

In the end, the Knicks lost 111-102 to the Magic. This is now their third-straight loss to start the 2026-27 NBA season. They got smothered by the 76ers in a 106-100 heartbreak, followed by a 107-103 clutch beating by the Boston Celtics .

The Knicks are now the first defending champions to start their campaign with a 0-3 record since 2011-12. Dirk Nowitzki and the Mavericks were the last team to do the same, per ESPN Insights.

So, what does this mean for the Knicks? Historically speaking, the fates are not on their side. See, the era of parity in the NBA is at an all-time high, and there is no incentive to tank given the contract pressures of Josh Hart and Karl-Anthony Towns.

They will also have a rough schedule. Their next games have them facing the Detroit Pistons , Chicago Bulls , Philadelphia 76ers, Brooklyn Nets , Milwaukee Bucks , and Cleveland Cavaliers . Three of those teams could be easy wins, but changes need to happen for that to happen.

Compared side by side with the 2011-12 Mavericks, things don't look great for Brunson and the Knicks . That squad managed only 36 wins, though it was a lockout-shortened season with just 66 games. Eventually, this Mavericks squad would come crashing down in the first round against the season runners-up, the Oklahoma City Thunder, led by Kevin Durant, James Harden, and Russell Westbrook.

There is no monolith archetype of defending champion in the NBA. The Knicks can stray away from these comparisons to the Nowitzki-led Mavericks. However, it will take a lot of willpower to do so.

Will the magic of New York save them again for a repeat, or was that all just reserved for the summer of 2026?
